prompt.criteria: Classify the failure into exactly one governed SOP recovery action: safe deterministic repair (AUTO_FIX), continued automated work (CONTINUE), a transient retry (RETRY), invalid plan assumptions (REPLAN), a genuine human decision (NEEDS_HUMAN), or a terminal automation stop (BLOCK).

reasoning_setting: the production SystemOne transport exposes no reasoning/thinking parameter; the endpoint's decision engine applies its own setting
sampling_setting: the production SystemOne transport exposes no sampling parameters; the endpoint's decision engine applies its own settings
cache_policy: no cache directive is sent; the endpoint default applies
notes: One attempt per case; no retry and no fallback. The production clef provider is called directly, so the adapter CLI's fallback chain cannot mask a first-pass failure.
Models are run one at a time; every model uses the same case order, request text, output cap, timeout, and cache policy.

oMLX exposes no version or model revision through /v1/models or /health; those fields are null. The SystemOne response reports input/output tokens only, so TTFT, decode speed, and model-load duration are null.
The production SystemOne transport sends no max-tokens field, so no output cap is applied; both models use the endpoint default identically.
This corpus exercises the six-action governed disposition contract. The production SEAM-004 change-risk checkpoint offers only LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/HUMAN and can only add NEEDS_HUMAN.
